steps.name: Block in the curled cat

lines.text: Let the blanket and the windowsill dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Optional: lightly chalk its outline first, from the transfer outline in Before you start, measuring from the canvas edges with a ruler.
Inside the outlined area. Its top is about 1 1/4 in from the top edge, and its right side is at the right edge; it's about 15 in wide and 7 in tall.
Paint: Mid gray.
Brush: 1/2 inch flat.
Start with one simple shape (an oval, a circle, or a rectangle). Then add the rest in curved pieces on each side, like ( ), smaller toward the edges.
It should leave a shape made of distinct curved segments with small gaps or overlaps between them.

steps.meant: A flat mid-gray curled cat shape lies on the blanket, with no shading, white patches, stripes, ears' pink or face.

steps.name: Shade the cat's shadow side
steps.part: The cat's shading and white patches

lines.text: Let the sleeping tabby cat and the blanket dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area. Its bottom is about 3 1/2 in from the bottom edge, and its left side is about 3 1/2 in from the left edge; it's about 7 in wide and 4 in tall.
The outline also runs under where the cat's stripes and pink ears, and the cat's sleeping face will go: paint straight through there.
The outline also reaches onto the sleeping tabby cat and the blue wall, painted already: there, only soften this paint into their edge and leave them showing.
Paint: Dark gray.
Brush: 1/2 inch flat.
Bend every stroke with the shape: from the top of each bump down along its curve, and around a round shape.
It should leave marks that bend with the shape, which is what makes it look round or sloped.

steps.meant: The gray cat has a dark underside, tail and fold behind its head, mid gray still on top. No white patches, stripes or face yet.

steps.name: Paint the white patches
steps.part: The cat's shading and white patches

lines.text: Let the sleeping tabby cat and the blanket dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area. Its bottom is about 3 1/2 in from the bottom edge, and its left side is about 3 1/2 in from the left edge; it's about 7 in wide and 4 in tall.
The outline also runs under where the cat's stripes and pink ears will go: paint straight through there.
The outline also reaches onto the yellow knit blanket and the sleeping tabby cat, painted already: there, only soften this paint into their edge and leave them showing.
Paint: Warm white.
Brush: #8 round.
Bend every stroke with the shape: from the top of each bump down along its curve, and around a round shape.
It should leave marks that bend with the shape, which is what makes it look round or sloped.
Leave what step 14 painted showing around these marks, as in the Result picture.
Warm white is much lighter than what it goes over: expect two or three thin coats, letting each dry.
Step back, squint, or take a photo to see it whole, and compare the big shapes with the picture.

steps.meant: The gray cat now has a white muzzle, a white patch on its side and two white front paws. No stripes, pink ears or face yet.
